newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand slips ahead of forex D-Day.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand slips ahead of forex D-Day.

text.p: The South African rand slipped to its lowest level since February 5 on Monday as banks continued to stock up on dollars ahead of a milestone relaxation of foreign exchange control from July 1.

But there was no panic, and despite an easier rand and weak gold price, financial markets remained in generally upbeat mood. Most analysts expect the relaxation of controls to occur without triggering a big capital flight or run on the rand.

Individual South Africans will be allowed to invest 200,000 rand ($44,000) offshore from Tuesday, the first time they have been able to export capital since the imposition of current exchange control regulations in 1961.
At 1230 GMT, the rand was trading at 4.5235/5365 against the dollar from 4.5145/5175 late on Friday.
"There's a little bit of pressure ahead of tomorrow's exchange controls. Everyone is looking to pick up dollars," a trader said.

The central Reserve Bank predicts that the measure will spark outflows of three to five billion rand. Some economists put it slightly higher, but few expect outflows to exceed 10 billion rand in the coming months.

With official foreign reserves standing at a record 21.8 billion rand at May 31 and expected to have increased further in June, traders are sanguine the central bank has the ammunition to smooth any short-term currency shocks.
As a result, the markets are looking beyond the easing of capital controls to an expected interest rate cut, possibly around September.

Rate cut hopes have been fuelled by a better-than-expected fall in the annual consumer inflation rate to 9.5 percent in May from 9.9 percent in April, coupled with a decline in both M3 money supply and private credit extension last month.
The expectation of cheaper credit continued to propel the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Monday, where both the industrial and all-share indices climbed to new record highs.
